thread.title: GWU Hospital nurses request NLRB to overturn policy blocking union decertification vote
thread.title_full: GWU Hospital nurses request NLRB to overturn policy blocking union decertification vote

author: Old Dominion News
title: GWU Hospital nurses request NLRB to overturn policy blocking union decertification vote
text:
A nurse at George Washington University Hospital has asked the National Labor Relations Board on June 3 to stop using its “blocking charge” policy, which is preventing hospital employees from voting in an election to remove District of Columbia Nurses Association union officials. The request follows a petition signed by hundreds of registered nurses and healthcare professionals seeking to decertify the union.
In April, GWU hospital workers led by nurse Elizabeth Abraha filed a decertification petition with the National Labor Relations Board. The agency is responsible for enforcing the National Labor Relations Act, including administering elections to certify or decertify unions. After Abraha’s petition was submitted, DCNA union leaders filed unfair labor practice charges against the hospital in an effort to block the election.
Abraha’s Request for Review argues that NLRB regional officials accepted these charges without due process, stating her petition was suspended “based on ULP charge proceedings without holding a public hearing or even permitting Petitioner to review the charges.” She contends that allowing a third party to unilaterally halt an election violates Section 9 of the NLRA, which requires investigation and a secret ballot if there is a question of representation.
The Request for Review also claims that NLRB regional staff denied due process by refusing hearings or access to information about the charges used as grounds for blocking the vote. It states that nothing in federal law grants authority for rules preventing worker-requested decertification elections.
“The text of the NLRA unambiguously states that employees have the right to hold decertification elections to remove an unwanted union from their workplace,” said Mark Mix, president of National Right to Work Foundation. “The NLRB should be defending employee free choice, not inventing policies that protect incumbent union bosses from being voted out by rank-and-file workers,” Mix added. “Ending the biased Biden-era blocking charge policy would be one of the most pro-worker changes the new Board majority could and should take.”
The National Right to Work Legal Defense and Education Foundation provides free legal aid and advocates for workers’ rights regarding compulsory unionism through litigation and education efforts, according to its official website.
summary: In April, GWU hospital workers led by nurse Elizabeth Abraha filed a decertification petition with the National Labor Relations Board. After Abraha’s petition was submitted, DCNA union leaders filed unfair labor practice charges against the hospital in an effort to block the election.
